actual_scope: At p=19, beta0=-1/2, bandwidth 2, and t_i=i, what 1-norm does direct elimination give for the inverse of the normalized six-by-six Schur section, and is it strictly below 3938?
scope_change_reason: The inverse infinity norm lies strictly between 18/5 and 361/100. The named next step is the induced 1-norm of the same inverse.
bottleneck_link: The Neumann 1-norm ceiling on this section is 3938. Direct elimination puts the inverse 1-norm strictly between 281/100 and 282/100.
stop_rule: Stop once the inverse 1-norm is enclosed. Do not enclose the 2-norm.
evidence: research/gaussian-origin-inverse-one reuses the denominator-10^12 midpoint inverse. The interval residual has 1-norm below 10^{-11}, and the inverse 1-norm lies strictly between 281/100 and 282/100.
